newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait to shed stake in shipbuilding firm.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait to shed stake in shipbuilding firm.

text.p: Kuwait plans to sell 105 million of its 108 million shares in Kuwait Shipbuilding and Repairyard Co (KSRC) in a two-stage privatisation, the official Kuwait News Agency reported on Thursday.

"Kuwait Investment Authority (KIA) has announced its intention to offer 40 million shares of its own stake and of that of (state-owned) Kuwait Oil Tanker Company (KOTC) in KSRC in a public auction," said the agency.
KIA, the state investment arm, also plans to shed 65 million KSRC shares in a public offering at a price to be determined after the auction, said the agency without giving a date.
The starting price for the March auction, whose exact date is yet to be set, will be 206 fils ($0.68) per share, said the agency. KSRC's share closed at 206 fils on Wednesday.
There are 1,000 fils to the dinar.
The agency did not specify the amount of KSRC shares held by KOTC or KIA individually, but said their total stake amounts to 108 million shares. KSRC has 135.1 million subscribed shares.
KSRC's net profit fell to 840,000 dinars in calender 1995 from 984,000 dianrs in the previous year. The firm did not give dividends in both years. KSRC was established in 1974.

Since the mobilisation of a wide-ranging privatisation plan in 1994, KIA has sold stakes in 18 local firms for over $2 billion in the first phase of the plan which also involves 36 concerns worth $3 billion.
A second stage of the plan involves sheding state holdings in public services such as water, electricity and telecommunications.
Only nationals of the Gulf Cooperation Council countries -- Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Oman, and Bahrain -- can trade shares of Kuwaiti firms.
